band: band 12 of 12 -- skew/degenerate shapes: lam or mu (or nu) with a repeated part, hooks, single rows, single columns, rectangles, and all near-degenerate boundary data, at W = |nu| <= 60
target: King-Tollu-Toumazet (2004) positivity conjecture: a strictly negative coefficient of the stretched LR polynomial P(n) = c(n*nu; n*lam, n*mu)
result: NO counterexample. Band 12 is provably free of negative coefficients at EVERY weight, not merely in the enumerated window: every band-12 triple has dim Q <= 2. Absence of a counterexample proves nothing about the KTT conjecture and is NOT evidence for it.

band_definition.ambient: r = 4 hive polytopes Q(lam,mu,nu) in R^3 (Knutson-Tao), lam,mu,nu partitions with at most 4 parts, |lam|+|mu|=|nu| = W
band_definition.degeneracy_predicate_deg_p: p empty, OR p has a repeated positive part (covers every rectangle a^k with k>=2 and every column 1^k with k>=2), OR p is a hook (a,1^k) with k>=0 (covers every single row (a) and the column (1))
enumeration_filters: lam contained in nu and mu contained in nu componentwise -- a NECESSARY condition for Q nonempty (LR cone), so nothing with P not identically zero is discarded
lam <= mu lexicographically -- c(nu;lam,mu) = c(nu;mu,lam), so L(n) and hence P, V, h* are identical for the two orderings

counts.note: the census is the FULL exhaustive r=4 census for W<=60; band-12 membership is tracked as a flag, so both the band numbers and the full-space numbers are exact

extremes.max_normalized_volume_band12: none -- band 12 contains NO dim-3 hive polytope, so V = 0 for every band-12 triple

structural_theorem_width_lemma.statement: For r = 4 the constraint matrix A is the same 18x3 matrix for every triple and only b moves. Among the 18 rows both +d and -d occur for each of the six directions d in {e1, e2, e3, e2-e1, e3-e1, e3-e2}, and the resulting slab widths are EXACTLY: width(e1) = min(lam1-lam2, nu1-nu2); width(e2) = min(mu1-mu2, lam3-lam4); width(e3) = min(mu3-mu4, nu3-nu4); width(e2-e1) = lam2-lam3; width(e3-e1) = nu2-nu3; width(e3-e2) = mu2-mu3.
structural_theorem_width_lemma.corollary: dim Q = 3 FORCES lam1>lam2>lam3>lam4>=0, mu1>mu2>mu3>mu4>=0, nu1>nu2>nu3>nu4>=0, i.e. lam, mu, nu must all be STRICT as length-4 vectors. Every band-12 partition (empty / repeated part / hook) fails strictness, so every band-12 triple has dim Q <= 2, whence P(n) = A n^2 + B n + 1 (or lower degree) with A, B > 0: a negative coefficient is IMPOSSIBLE in band 12, at every weight.

reeve_indicator.criterion: for a 3-dim lattice polytope a_1 < 0 iff V > 3*(c + i), where c = #(Q cap Z^3) and i = #(int Q cap Z^3); equivalently 6*a_1 = 11 + 2*h*_1 - h*_2 + 2*h*_3, so negativity needs h*_2 > 11 + 2*h*_1 + 2*h*_3 (Reeve T_q has h* = (1,0,q-1,0) and a_1 = 2 - q/6 < 0 iff q >= 13)
reeve_indicator.finding: over the whole exhaustive W<=60 census, every hive polytope with h*_1 = 0 (exactly c = 4 = dim+1 lattice points) has normalized volume V = 1, i.e. it is a UNIMODULAR simplex. No Reeve tetrahedron T_q with q >= 2 occurs as an r=4 hive polytope for W <= 60. The largest normalized volume seen anywhere is 312 (lam = mu = [16,10,4], nu = [24,18,12,6]) with record h*_2 = 193 -- far from the negativity threshold.

check_7_positivity_for_dim_le_2.statement: the step 'dim Q <= 2 => no negative coefficient' is proved, not assumed, and does NOT need Q to be a lattice polytope
check_7_positivity_for_dim_le_2.proof: P(n) = L_Q(n) is a genuine polynomial (the stretched LR function is polynomial), so P(0) = 1. dim 0 gives P = 1; dim 1 gives P = An+1 with A = normalized length > 0. For dim 2 write P = An^2+Bn+1; Ehrhart-Macdonald reciprocity gives L_{int Q}(n) = P(-n) = An^2-Bn+1, so 2Bn = #(boundary lattice points of nQ) >= 0 for all n >= 1, whence B >= 0, and A = area > 0. No coefficient is ever strictly negative.
check_7_positivity_for_dim_le_2.consequence: band 12 is negativity-free at EVERY weight, not merely W <= 60, and in fact the conclusion extends to the strictly larger set of ALL triples in which lam, mu or nu fails to be strictly decreasing as a length-4 vector.
